newsitem.title: UK: Abbey's Birch denies in favour of NatWest's bid.
newsitem.headline: Abbey's Birch denies in favour of NatWest's bid.

text.p: Abbey National chief executive Peter Birch on Thursday denied press reports that he had personally been in favour of a merger approach made to Abbey by National Westminster Bank Plc which was revealed earlier this month.

Asked if he had been in favour, Birch replied, "Categorically no", adding that the Abbey board had been unanimous in rejecting the approach -- "The board of Abbey National made a decision that it does not want to embark on discussions with anyone," Birch told Reuters in an interview.
Birch said Abbey wanted to retain its own independence and continue its good track record for creating shareholder value as an efficient provider of financial services.

"We want to move forward and grow our own business and not be involved in surgery for someone else, we don't know if we're good at surgery because we've never tried but we are good at growing businesses and we want to grow our own," Birch said.

The revelation that NatWest had approached Abbey has led to a mass of speculation over other merger partners for troubled NatWest which on Thursday announced the results of an embarrassing report into a 77 million pounds ($128 million) loss in its derivatives trading.
Also on Thursday, Abbey announced it bought financial services group Cater Allen for 191 million pounds which will double its offshore banking and stock lending businesses.
Birch said Abbey will continue to look for acquisitions that will add to shareholder value but that these will not necessarily be in its traditional business areas.
